title: Exact condensed induction for a split profinite coset projection
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent site of profinite sets [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$, let $\mathcal A_P(A)$ be the category of internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $H$ be a closed subgroup of $P$. Give the coset space $X=\{pH:p\in P\}$ its quotient topology, and assume it is profinite and that the projection $q:P\to X$ admits a continuous section $s:X\to P$ with $q s=1_X$.

For a profinite test set $S$, write $P_S=C(S,P)$ and $H_S=C(S,H)$. The group algebra $A(S)[P_S]$ consists of finite formal sums $\sum a_p[p]$, with $[p][p']=[pp']$. For $M\in\mathcal A_H(A)$, form the presheaf of $A$-modules
$$S\longmapsto A(S)[P_S]\otimes_{A(S)[H_S]}M(S),$$
with restrictions induced by those of $A,M$ and precomposition of continuous maps. Let $\operatorname{Ind}_H^P M$ be its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Left multiplication on $P_S$ induces a condensed $P$-action on this sheafification. This construction is an additive exact functor $\operatorname{Ind}_H^P:\mathcal A_H(A)\to\mathcal A_P(A)$, where exact means preservation of short exact sequences of internal equivariant modules. It is left adjoint to restriction $\operatorname{Res}_H^P$. The adjunction sends $F:\operatorname{Ind}_H^P M\to N$ to $m\mapsto F([1]\otimes m)$; its inverse sends an $H$-equivariant map $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}_H^P N$ to $[p]\otimes m\mapsto p\cdot f(m)$ and then factors through sheafification. No finiteness assumption on $X$ and no discreteness assumption on $M$ is made.

proof.text: The closed subgroup $H$ is profinite, with its inherited compact Hausdorff topology and clopen basis. By [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], with second group trivial, $\mathcal A_H(A)$ and $\mathcal A_P(A)$ are abelian. Apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] to $K(S)=C(S,J)$ for $J=H,P$ on our small profinite site: forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels and detects zero. It creates images as kernels of cokernels and reflects isomorphisms: a map with invertible underlying map has zero kernel and cokernel. Thus it reflects exactness by applying this criterion to the image-to-kernel map. These applications use finite limits, finite jointly surjective covers, and the trivial action on $A$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-tensor-induction-adjunction] to $A,P,H$. It gives exactly the stated sheafification functor $L$, its action and map formulas, additivity, and $L\dashv\operatorname{Res}_H^P$ with the required two transposes. The coset section is unnecessary for this part.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-coset-tensor-normal-form] to the given $q,s$. For an equivariant map $u:M\to N$, put $K=\ker u$. Its sections are $K(S)=\ker u_S$ by [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. The natural normal form identifies $B_u(S)$ with coefficientwise $u_S$ on finite-support sums, so $B_K(S)\to B_M(S)$ is injective and has image exactly $\ker B_u(S)$. This is an identification of presheaf kernels, including restrictions that merge indices. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], sheafifying preserves this kernel. Thus $LK$ is the underlying kernel of $Lu$; its equivariant comparison is a kernel as well by the action-site statement. This proves preservation of kernels without assuming sectionwise surjectivity of epimorphisms.

proof.text: For $u:M'\to M$ with cokernel $v:M\to Q$, a map $a:LM\to N$ satisfying $aLu=0$ transposes by step 2 to $b:M\to\operatorname{Res}N$ with $bu=0$. The unique $c:Q\to\operatorname{Res}N$ with $cv=b$ transposes to the unique $d:LQ\to N$ with $dLv=a$. Also $LvLu=L(vu)=0$ by additivity. Hence $Lv$ is a cokernel of $Lu$. A short exact sequence is a kernel/cokernel pair in these abelian categories; kernel preservation from step 3 and this cokernel property preserve both descriptions. The finite-support normal forms allow arbitrary $C(S,X)$ and arbitrary coefficient sections, so neither finiteness nor discreteness was imposed.
